What changes with voxel size?

NUMERIC AXIS · 0 / 0.08 / 0.20

Zero represents the original, unfiltered input. The horizontal gaps follow the actual voxel cell sizes. These three observations describe this experiment; they do not establish a general relationship for other captures.

Method and limits

ONLY THE STARTING SPARSE INPUT IS FILTERED
  1. Reuse the screened Insta360 4× recovery: 320 calibrated views, 960 × 540 undistorted photographs, and the same 40 fixed validation frames. Data factor 1 avoids another image downsample. Pinhole projection is correct for these already-undistorted images; the upstream reconstruction used estimated OPENCV_FISHEYE intrinsics.
  2. Partition the original sparse points into cells of size 0.08 or 0.20 around a fixed median origin. Within each cell retain one existing point: longest track first, then lower existing reprojection error, then point ID. Sizes are arbitrary COLMAP model units, not meters. Retained coordinates, colors and tracks are unchanged; no rounding or centroid averaging is applied.
  3. Remove deleted points’ observation references from a separate, complete COLMAP model copy. Validate its camera poses, calibration, surviving tracks and source-image identities. Keep all original files.
  4. Train official gsplat 1.5.3 for 30,000 steps on the RTX 4090, using seed 42, batch size 1, SH3, packed rasterization, SSIM weight 0.2 and the default growth/pruning strategy. Camera, appearance and depth-loss optimization remain disabled. Save and evaluate at 7,000 and 30,000 steps.
  5. Validate the checkpoint, complete SH3 PLY and all 40 native predictions, then compare the same viewpoints and saved metrics.

Voxel filtering lowers initial spatial density and changes nearest-neighbor Gaussian sizes. It also removes coincident points: the original input had 714 zero initial scales, and its final checkpoint had 712 rows with negative-infinite log scales. The finite original PLY omits those 712 rows explicitly. Both filtered inputs start with strictly positive scales. Any improvement therefore combines thinning with removal of these degenerate seeds.

Default densification can add Gaussians again, so a smaller points3D.bin does not cap the final Gaussian count or guarantee a faster or more accurate reconstruction. Image-quality scores and file integrity alone cannot confirm faithful room geometry. Inspect the same-view images, coverage gaps and complete models.
